item.text: The mapper already carries WPScan references, dates, classification, and fix versions, but it expands every CVE reference into a separate record and drops Enterprise fields. The model already supports summaries, CVSS values, and optional metadata, so I’m adding those to the existing WPScan content while retaining one record keyed by the first CVE reference.

The mapping now produces a single record per vulnerability using the first CVE reference, preserves ordered URLs and UTC timestamps, and fills the existing WPScan summary/CVSS fields. I’m checking the empty metadata serialization too, since `omitempty` would otherwise erase the required empty map from output.

# Checkpoint

Task: resolve WPScan Enterprise field handling in WordPress vulnerability ingestion.

Repository inspection found the mapper in `detector/wordpress.go`. The mapper now emits one result per vulnerability using the first CVE reference, preserves ordered URLs and UTC dates, carries description/classification/fix data, maps CVSS fields, and stores PoC/introduced version in optional metadata. The optional metadata field serializes empty maps as `{}`.

Regression coverage was added for enriched and basic/null payloads. Verification passed: `go test ./detector ./models`.

item.text:
Implemented WPScan Enterprise field handling in [wordpress.go](/app/detector/wordpress.go). Records now use the first CVE reference, preserve ordered URLs and UTC timestamps, and carry the summary, classification, fix version, CVSS metrics, and optional PoC and introduced version. Empty optional metadata serializes as `{}`.

Added regression coverage for enriched and basic payloads in [wordpress_test.go](/app/detector/wordpress_test.go).

Verified with `go test ./detector ./models`; `git diff --check` also passed.
